No Result View All Result Home News Politics Business Sport Football Health Entertainment Education Opinion Editorial Columns Others LeVogue Magazine Conferences National Economy Contact Us Hausa Edition Home News Politics Business Sport Football Health Entertainment Education Opinion Editorial Columns Others LeVogue Magazine Conferences National Economy Contact Us No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Lawyers Ask Court To Suspend NNPCL Executive Pending Corruption Probe by Olakunle Olasanmi 6 seconds ago in News Share on WhatsApp Share on Facebook Share on X Telegram Four lawyers have approached the High Court of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Abuja, seeking an ex parte order to suspend the Executive Vice President, Downstream, of the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL), Mumuni Dagazau, pending the conclusion of an investigation by the House of Representatives Committee on Petroleum Resources (Downstream).
The suit, marked M/15759/2026, was filed by Ejike Onukaogu, Gloria Ezeji, Daniel Edeachi and Akor Friday, who want the court to determine whether Dagazau can lawfully remain in office while facing legislative scrutiny over allegations of corruption, money laundering, abuse of office and related matters.
In an originating summons, the claimants also asked the court to determine whether President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has a constitutional obligation to take steps to suspend the NNPCL executive in the interest of transparency, accountability and the integrity of the ongoing investigation.
They argued that temporarily relieving Dagazau of his duties would help protect the investigation from actual or perceived interference.
The lawyers contended that his continued exercise of the powers attached to the office, under the circumstances outlined in the suit, raised concerns that warranted judicial intervention.
Among the reliefs sought, the claimants asked the court to restrain Dagazau from performing the duties and functions of Executive Vice President, Downstream, pending the conclusion of the House of Representatives committee’s investigation.
They also sought an order directing the President, the NNPCL Board of Directors or any other appropriate authority, as determined by the court, to take the necessary steps to suspend the executive while the investigation lasted.
The claimants further asked the court to determine whether his continued occupation of the office was consistent with the principles of fairness, accountability and the protection of the public interest.
They urged the court to consider whether interim measures were necessary to safeguard the legislative investigation and preserve public confidence in the institutions responsible for managing the country’s petroleum resources.
The suit was filed by their counsel, Samuel Momoh. No date has been fixed for its hearing.
Speaking with journalists at the premises of the Federal High Court in Abuja, Onukaogu, who represented the group, said the allegations were serious enough to warrant Dagazau’s temporary withdrawal from office while the investigation continued.
He said the suit, filed on Wednesday, was intended to protect the integrity of the investigation initiated by the House of Representatives Committee on the Petroleum Downstream Sector.
Onukaogu clarified that the lawyers were neither seeking Dagazau’s resignation nor suggesting that he was guilty of any wrongdoing. Rather, he said, they wanted him to step aside to promote transparency and public confidence in the investigative process.
“Nobody has proved any guilt against him. So he should step aside in order to preserve the integrity of the investigation against him,” he said.
